relationships.subject: IL-1β
relationships.evidence_quote: It forms a positive feedback loop through activating the NLRP3 inflammasome, resulting in sustained amplification of the inflammatory response.

relationships.subject: IL-6
relationships.evidence_quote: Via binding to the gp130 receptor, it activates the STAT3 pathway

relationships.subject: IL-10
relationships.evidence_quote: IL-10 inhibits the excessive activation of immune cells and promotes the expression of brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF).

relationships.subject: MMP-9
relationships.evidence_quote: including MMP-3 and MMP-9, which directly degrade myelin proteins and impair the integrity of nerve conduction

key_findings: Narrative review: pro-inflammatory ILs (IL-1β, IL-6, IL-17) drive nerve root demyelination and axonal injury in LDH via NLRP3, JAK-STAT3 and p38MAPK; IL-4/IL-10 are neuroprotective.
Translational barriers: lack of objective biomarkers and poor local drug delivery across the blood-nerve barrier.
